newsitem.title: GREECE: Bank of Greece cuts discount, overdraft rates.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Greece cuts discount, overdraft rates.

text.p: Greece's central bank will cut its discount and overdraft rates by 100 basis points, effective December 18, and lower the rate it pays commercial banks on interest bearing reserves on January 1, it said on Tuesday.
Its discount rate will fall to 16.5 from 17.5 percent and the overdraft rate will drop to 25 from 26 percent, it said in a statement.
Commercial banks' interest bearing reserves with the Bank of Greece will earn a lower 11.0 percent, down 150 basis points from 12.5 percent previously, effective January 1, 1997.
The Bank of Greece said the adjustments sought to bring the rates closer to its interbank intervention rate.

"The adjustment of the rate on interest bearing reserves was necessary to boost the effectiveness of this monetary policy instrument following the significant drop in deposit and lending rates since mid-1995," the central bank statement said.
